requirements.definition: The grammar for array-element is exactly data-ref. C924 supplies the additional rank-zero and final-subscript-list restrictions; 9.4.2 owns data-ref and part-ref formation.

pending.data-ref-array-element-form: PENDING positive-control source with INTEGER a(3)=[5,7,9] and designator a(2) used in a value context. The independent literal oracle is 7, proving scalar element selection; the data-ref grammar and final subscript prerequisites are separately satisfied.

requirements.title: Every part reference in an array element has rank zero and the last part reference has a subscript list
requirements.definition: For an R917 array-element, every part-ref in the data-ref shall have rank zero, and the last part-ref shall contain a subscript list. This excludes array sections and whole arrays from the array-element category while allowing component chains whose parent parts are scalar or are reduced to scalar elements.

pending.all-part-refs-rank-zero: PENDING positive-control source: scalar parent with array component c(3), use parent%c(2) after assigning distinct literals; oracle literal is the second component value. Non-vacuous because each preceding part-ref is scalar and the selected element differs from neighbours.
pending.last-part-ref-has-subscript-list: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: declared INTEGER a(3), attempt to use a as an array-element context requiring R917; repair by adding (2) and observe literal 7 from [5,7,9]. The cause to record is missing final subscript list, not undeclared name or type failure.
pending.nonzero-rank-part-ref-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: derived-type array parent arr(2)%c(3), attempt arr(1:2)%c(1) as an array element; repair to arr(1)%c(1) with literal oracle from distinct parent elements. The non-vacuous distinction is the section parent rank versus scalar parent.

requirements.title: An array section is a data reference with optional substring range or a complex part designator
requirements.definition: The grammar for array-section admits a data-ref, optionally followed by a parenthesized substring-range, or a complex-part-designator. C925 and C926 supply rank and character restrictions; 9.4.4 owns complex-part-designator details.

pending.data-ref-section-form: PENDING positive-control source with INTEGER a(4)=[1,2,3,4] and section a(1:4:2). Oracle is SHAPE [2] and values [1,3], proving array rather than scalar selection.
pending.data-ref-with-substring-range-form: PENDING positive-control source with CHARACTER(4) c(3)=["abcd","wxyz","lmno"] and section c(:)(2:3). Oracle is SHAPE [3] and element literals ["bc","xy","mn"], proving substring-range application to each selected element.
pending.complex-part-designator-section-form: PENDING positive-control source with COMPLEX z(2)=[(1,10),(2,20)] and section designator z%re or z%im. Oracle is real array values [1,2] or [10,20]; non-vacuous because the complex array is not scalar and the part designator controls which component is selected.

requirements.title: An array section has exactly one nonzero-rank source and must be justified by section subscripts, another nonzero-rank part, or an array complex part
requirements.definition: For an R918 array-section, exactly one part-ref shall have nonzero rank. In addition, either the final part-ref has a section-subscript-list with nonzero rank, another part-ref has nonzero rank, or the complex-part-designator is an array. This catalogue records the complex-part wording as source-sensitive: the complex-part alternative is admitted through 9.4.4, while data-ref rank and part-ref rank remain owned by 9.4.2.

pending.exactly-one-nonzero-rank-part-ref: PENDING positive-control source: a(1:3) or scalar_parent%array_field(1:3), with oracle SHAPE [3] and distinct values, where exactly one final part-ref is nonzero rank.
pending.final-section-subscript-list-nonzero-ran: PENDING positive-control source using a final part-ref section list with a triplet or vector subscript, e.g. a(1:4:2); oracle SHAPE [2] and values [first, third] establish nonzero rank.
pending.nonfinal-part-ref-nonzero-rank: PENDING positive-control source: array parent arr(1:2)%scalar_field where final part-ref is scalar and the nonfinal part-ref supplies rank. Oracle is SHAPE [2] and two distinct component literals; 9.4.2 owns the data-ref rank calculation.
pending.complex-part-designator-array: PENDING positive-control source: COMPLEX array z(2) and z%im as an array section. Oracle is real array values from imaginary parts, with z scalar control nearby to avoid accepting only scalar complex parts.
pending.zero-rank-section-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: source shaped as an array-section alternative but all part-refs are rank zero, such as scalar complex z%re or a(1) where an array section is required; repair to z_array%re or a(1:1). Literal SHAPE [1] in repaired source is the oracle, not address identity.
pending.multiple-nonzero-rank-parts-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: derived-type array parent with array component, attempt arr(:)%c(:) so two part-refs have nonzero rank; repair one side to scalar subscript and use SHAPE/literal SUM oracle. Reported cause must be the C925/C919 rank conflict, not unrelated component lookup.

requirements.title: A subscript is a scalar integer expression
requirements.definition: The grammar for subscript is scalar-int-expr. The value bounds of a subscript in an array element are specified separately by 9.5.3.1 p2, and section-subscript rank effects are specified by 9.4.2 and 9.5.3.4.

pending.literal-scalar-int-subscript: PENDING positive-control source: INTEGER a(3)=[4,5,6], use a(2) with oracle literal 5. Non-vacuous because adjacent elements differ.
pending.variable-scalar-int-subscript: PENDING positive-control source: INTEGER i=3 and a(3)=[4,5,6], use a(i) with oracle literal 6 after proving i is assigned. Non-vacuous because changing i changes the selected value.
pending.noninteger-or-nonscalar-subscript-reject: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: use a(1.0) or another scalar noninteger expression where all declarations otherwise legal; repair only the subscript expression to scalar integer 1 or 2 and observe the corresponding literal element. Cause must be scalar-int-expr failure, not bounds. Rank-one integer array contrasts such as a([1,2]) are vector-subscript/rank-classification cases owned by C924/C925/C929 and C913 dependencies, not this R919 plan.

requirements.title: A multiple subscript is an at sign followed by an integer expression
requirements.definition: The grammar for multiple-subscript is @ followed by int-expr. C927 requires that expression to be a rank-one array, and 9.5.3.2 owns the expansion into consecutive dimensions.

pending.at-token-present: PENDING positive-control source: rank-two INTEGER a(2,2) with distinct values, use a(@[1,2]) as the element equivalent to a(1,2). Oracle is the literal at position (1,2), making the @ form non-vacuous.
pending.int-expr-after-at: PENDING positive-control source: INTEGER vector v=[2,1], use a(@v) with oracle equal to a(2,1). Non-vacuous because reversing v changes the selected literal.
pending.missing-at-token-rejected: PENDING source-classification contrast, not a diagnostic expectation: with rank-two INTEGER a holding distinct values and rank-one INTEGER v=[1,2], use a(@v) as the R920 multiple-subscript element equivalent to a(1,2), and contrast it with a(v,1) where the same vector is an R925/C929 vector-subscript producing a rank-one section. Oracles are the scalar literal at a(1,2) versus SHAPE [2] and the two literals from column 1; any omitted-@ rejection in a scalar-element or rank-accounting context is attributed to C913/C924/C925 dependencies, not to R920 form.

requirements.title: A section subscript is one of five subscript forms
requirements.definition: The grammar for section-subscript admits exactly: subscript, multiple-subscript, subscript-triplet, multiple-subscript-triplet, or vector-subscript. Rank contribution and sequence semantics are owned by 9.4.2 p2, 9.5.3.2, and 9.5.3.4.

pending.subscript-alternative: PENDING positive-control source: a(2,:) on rank-two array, with scalar integer first section-subscript. Oracle SHAPE of result and SUM over distinct row values prove scalar dimension reduction.

pending.subscript-triplet-alternative: PENDING positive-control source: a(1:5:2), oracle SHAPE [3] and values at positions 1,3,5.

pending.vector-subscript-alternative: PENDING positive-control source: INTEGER v(2)=[3,1], use a(v). Oracle values [a(3),a(1)] in that order; non-vacuous because vector order differs from triplet order.

requirements.definition: A vector-subscript shall be an integer array expression of rank one. This constraint establishes type and rank only; it does not own bounds of the resulting values, definedness of expression elements, duplicate-element definability, or finalization restrictions.

pending.scalar-int-expr-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: in a context requiring vector-subscript classification rather than scalar subscript, replace rank-one vector v with scalar i; repair back to v and observe SHAPE [size(v)]. Cause must distinguish scalar subscript from vector subscript.
pending.rank-two-array-expression-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: use INTEGER m(1,2) as a vector subscript; repair to rank-one [m(1,1),m(1,2)] and observe ordered literals.
pending.noninteger-array-expression-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: use REAL vector rv as subscript expression; repair to INTEGER vector iv with same values and observe ordered literals. Type, not rank or bounds, is isolated.

requirements.title: The second subscript is required for a subscript triplet in the last dimension of an assumed-size array
requirements.definition: For an R922 subscript-triplet in the last dimension of an assumed-size array, the second subscript shall not be omitted. The assumed-size property and absence of a last upper bound are owned by 8.5.8.5.

pending.assumed-size-last-dimension-upper-presen: PENDING positive-control source: dummy INTEGER a(3,*), use a(:,1:2) or a(1,1:2) with explicit second subscript in the last dimension and a caller providing distinct values. Oracle is fixed SHAPE/literal SUM over the selected first two columns.
pending.nonlast-dimension-omission-control: PENDING positive-control source: assumed-size dummy a(3,*), use a(:,1) or a(1:3,1) where the omitted upper bound is only in the nonlast explicit-shape dimension and the last dimension has scalar subscript 1; oracle derives first-dimension extent from declaration.
pending.ordinary-array-omission-control: PENDING positive-control source: explicit-shape a(5), use a(2:) with omitted second subscript; oracle selected values through known upper bound, proving C930 is limited to assumed-size last dimension.
pending.assumed-size-last-dimension-upper-omitte: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: assumed-size dummy a(*) or a(3,*), attempt a(:) or a(1,:) in the last dimension; repair by writing an explicit upper subscript such as :n supplied by a separate dummy. Repaired oracle uses caller literals within the explicit range; do not infer shape from the assumed-size array.

requirements.title: The second integer expression is required for a final multiple subscript triplet of an assumed-size array
requirements.definition: If a multiple-subscript-triplet is the last section-subscript in the section-subscript-list of an assumed-size array, the second int-expr shall appear. This is the multiple-triplet counterpart of C930 and depends on 9.5.3.2 for expansion.

pending.assumed-size-final-multiple-triplet-seco: PENDING positive-control source: assumed-size dummy with a final multiple-subscript-triplet such as @[1,1]:[2,2] where the second int-expr appears; oracle uses finite expanded coordinates and caller literals.
pending.nonfinal-multiple-triplet-omission-contr: PENDING positive-control source: assumed-size array of rank at least three where a multiple-subscript-triplet with omitted second int-expr is not the last section-subscript; oracle shows selected coordinates before the last explicit dimension.
pending.ordinary-array-multiple-triplet-omission: PENDING positive-control source: explicit-shape array with final @[...] : omission relying on known upper bounds; oracle computes shape from declared constants.
pending.assumed-size-final-multiple-triplet-seco: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: assumed-size dummy and final multiple-subscript-triplet @[...] : with omitted second int-expr; repair by adding a conformable second vector. Repaired source has literal selected coordinates; failure cause must be C931, not C928 conformability.

requirements.title: Array elements are scalar, array sections are arrays, and substring ranges apply elementwise
requirements.definition: An array element is scalar. An array section is an array. If a substring-range appears in an array-section, each element of the result is the designated substring of the corresponding element of the array section.

pending.array-element-is-scalar: PENDING positive-control source: INTEGER a(3) and scalar assignment x=a(2), with oracle literal equal to element 2 and a compile/source check that scalar context admits x. Non-vacuous because a(1:2) would be rank one.
pending.array-section-is-array: PENDING positive-control source: INTEGER a(3), section a(1:3:2), and SHAPE/SIZE oracle [2]/2 plus SUM over distinct elements. Non-vacuous because scalar element a(1) lacks shape [2].
pending.substring-range-applies-to-each-section-: PENDING positive-control source: CHARACTER(4) c(2)=["abcd","wxyz"], section c(:)(2:3), oracle SHAPE [2] and literals ["bc","xy"]. Non-vacuous because both elements have distinct substrings.

requirements.title: An array element subscript value is within the bounds of its dimension
requirements.definition: For an array element, the value of each subscript shall be within the bounds for its dimension. This is a value restriction: constant out-of-bounds sources can be planned as source-diagnostic candidates, while variable-valued subscripts require execution or other context to establish the actual value. This p2 rule is for array elements; array-section triplet and vector value rules are owned by 9.5.3.4.

pending.constant-in-bounds-element: PENDING positive-control source: INTEGER a(2:4) with distinct literals and designator a(3); oracle is the literal assigned to bound value 3, showing the subscript is inside declared lower/upper bounds.
pending.constant-out-of-bounds-element-source-ca: PENDING diagnostic-policy/source pair: INTEGER a(2:4), use a(5) in an array-element value context; repair only the subscript to 4 and observe that element literal. Because p2 is unnumbered prose, any diagnostic expectation needs separate policy/adjudication even when the value is constant.
pending.runtime-valued-in-bounds-element: PENDING execution-source plan: INTEGER i assigned from a branch to value 3 before a( i ); oracle is the literal at a(3) and a reached-path marker. Non-vacuous because changing i to 2 changes the selected literal.
pending.runtime-valued-out-of-bounds-element: PENDING runtime-condition plan: source assigns a variable subscript from input or branch to a value outside bounds. The oracle is not undefined storage or compiler agreement; a future case must use an approved runtime diagnostic/status mechanism or remain source-only. No static diagnostic duty is claimed for the variable value.
